newsitem.title: PERU: Victim of Lima hostage crisis to sue Peru, Japan.
newsitem.headline: Victim of Lima hostage crisis to sue Peru, Japan.

text.p: A surgeon wounded during the storming of the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima by Marxist rebels plans to sue the Peruvian and Japanese governments for at least $500,000 in damages.
"We are going to sue Peru and Japan for the physical and moral damage caused to Dr. Emma Torres," her lawyer, Francisco Magallanes, told Reuters on Tuesday.

Torres, who lost movement in her left hand after it was struck by a stray bullet, was the only civilian injured during the fierce shootout on Dec. 17 when a Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) unit took over the residence. She says a police marksman shot her while she was helping frightened patients in a nearby clinic.

"A colleague told me that the bullet which entered through the window of the clinic was aimed at an MRTA member on the roof," she told Reuters from the Loayza Hospital in Lima, where she is being treated. "I was evacuating the patients to the corridors so the bullets would not hit them when I felt the impact."

The only other person believed hurt in the shootout was an MRTA member who was apparently shot in the leg. The MRTA is still holding 72 hostages at the residence nearly three months after the takeover.
Torres, whose husband is also in the hospital for a skin disease, has sent her four children to be looked after by family members in the northern Peruvian city of Trujillo.
